mission_goal: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas Ubuntu developer system

zero_cost_evidence.claim: NVIDIA Developer Program members have free access to hosted NIM API endpoints for prototyping; individual endpoints may be rate limited.
zero_cost_evidence.counterhypothesis: A configured credential can belong to a different billing or production context; request execution must still stay on the documented integrate.api.nvidia.com developer endpoint and emit a receipt.

request_bounds.claim: The exact serialized UTF-8 JSON request is capped at 2000000 bytes before runtime-environment snapshot, credential lookup or network access. This is a transport envelope, not a claim that bytes equal model tokens; model context limits remain provider- and profile-specific.
request_bounds.counterhypothesis: The provider can safely enforce its own context or body limit after authentication; falsified locally because a request above the runtime envelope reached the authenticated opener, while the repaired boundary rejects it before even reading the runtime environment and still accepts an exact-limit payload.

request_pre_serialization_bound.claim: Validated request text and message structure are checked against their exact default json.dumps size before the JSON document is materialized. The calculation includes the 66-byte fixed request envelope, 27-byte per-message structure, two-byte list separators and ensure_ascii escape width of every Unicode scalar. Requests above 2000000 bytes are rejected before serialization; the serialized UTF-8 byte check remains defense in depth.
request_pre_serialization_bound.internal_measurement: The repaired scalar-width function matched json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) for all 1112064 Unicode scalar values.
request_pre_serialization_bound.counterhypothesis: Exact string escape widths plus a small structural lower bound are sufficient before serialization; falsified locally because 54793 minimal alternating messages fit the old character estimate but their separators and closed-schema object envelopes exceed 2000000 bytes and reached full snapshot plus json.dumps allocation.

request_pre_lock_scalar_bound.claim: For exact built-in request strings, the sum of model, role and content character counts is a conservative lower bound on default JSON size. A sum above 2000000 therefore fails before the global execution lock; the exact escape-aware serialized-size calculation remains authoritative inside the protected snapshot path.
request_pre_lock_scalar_bound.counterhypothesis: The exact pre-serialization check is sufficient even when it runs under the process-wide lock; falsified locally because a request whose built-in text alone occupied 2000008 characters acquired and held the lock for validation scans before its inevitable size rejection.

request_pre_snapshot_cardinality_bound.claim: An exact built-in message list is rejected before snapshot allocation and before the process-wide execution lock when its cardinality exceeds 54792. The bound is rechecked at the snapshot boundary because caller-owned mutable input can change after early admission. Under required role alternation, the densest valid 54792-message request with a leading system message occupies 1999970 bytes with the smallest valid model; the next valid cardinality exceeds the 2000000-byte envelope.
request_pre_snapshot_cardinality_bound.counterhypothesis: Dividing the byte cap by the 32-byte smallest isolated message yields a safe maximum of 62500; falsified because that ignores required assistant-role width, list separators and the outer request envelope. A valid 54793-message conversation reached lock, snapshot and serialization before exact rejection.

output_token_budget.claim: Every v0.1 Chat Completions request explicitly caps combined generated reasoning and visible output at 4096 tokens. The number is a conservative local policy choice demonstrated in NVIDIA's reasoning example, not a claim that every task or model requires exactly 4096 tokens.
output_token_budget.counterhypothesis: Omitting max_tokens is safe because the provider default is an adequate bounded generation policy; falsified locally because the authenticated request contained no output budget, while NVIDIA documents max_tokens as the cap shared by reasoning and visible output and warns that budget exhaustion yields finish_reason length.

response_bounds.claim: A bounded read must request one sentinel byte beyond the accepted limit to distinguish an oversized response from a response that merely fills the limit.
response_bounds.counterhypothesis: Reading exactly the accepted limit is sufficient; falsified because HTTPResponse.read(amt) returns only up to amt bytes and therefore cannot prove end-of-body at that boundary.

payment_status_precedes_body.claim: A valid HTTP 402 status activates the current-budget-epoch payment hard stop immediately from response metadata; the adapter does not consume a non-200 body before status classification.
payment_status_precedes_body.counterhypothesis: Reading an error body before classifying its already received status is harmless; falsified because a stalled 402 body changed the outcome to incomplete_provider_response and suppressed the payment latch.

payment_hard_stop_atomicity.claim: For the single-instance v0.1 runtime, routing, authenticated execution and payment-latch publication form one process-serialized critical section; a waiting attempt re-evaluates the latch after the preceding receipt completes.
payment_hard_stop_atomicity.counterhypothesis: Independent preflight checks are sufficient for concurrent attempts; falsified locally because a second attempt reached the network while the first payment response was pending, before the shared hard-stop latch could be published.

bounded_payment_latch_state.claim: Payment-latch storage is limited to 1024 exact built-in string entries. Cardinality is checked immediately after the exact-set boundary and before element iteration, inventory membership, credential use or network access. At exactly 1024 entries, inventory fails closed as payment-latch capacity exhausted so a further provider response cannot append entry 1025; larger injected state is structurally rejected. The numeric limit is a local FRANK process-state budget, not a Python or protocol standard.
bounded_payment_latch_state.counterhypothesis: Exact built-in sets and strings sufficiently bound passive latch state; falsified locally because 1025 historical entries passed full element validation and reached authenticated routing without any cardinality policy. The repaired boundary routes with 1023 entries, fails closed without an opener at exactly 1024, and structurally rejects 1025 before element iteration.

payment_latch_evidence_separation.claim: Capability inventory reports payment_blocked_current_budget_epoch only when the exact provider and budget-epoch latch key exists. Storage-capacity exhaustion independently blocks eligibility as payment_latch_capacity_exhausted and cannot be represented as an observed HTTP 402 payment event.
payment_latch_evidence_separation.counterhypothesis: Every fail-closed route caused by payment-latch storage can be labeled as a current-epoch payment hard stop; falsified locally because 1024 unrelated historical keys produced payment_blocked_current_budget_epoch true and payment_required_hard_stop_active without the current provider/epoch key or any received HTTP 402.

payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.claim: Each capability inventory and its derived route evaluate payment-latch capacity and every provider membership against one bounded exact-set copy. A latch published after that snapshot belongs to the next inventory state and cannot partially alter the current claim.
payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.internal_measurement: A synchronized writer inserted the selected provider latch after capacity evaluation but before its membership test. Before repair, the same inventory mixed the earlier capacity state with the later blocked state; after repair, all rows represent the pre-write copy.
payment_latch_inventory_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Deriving route from one list of inventory rows is sufficient even when those rows read a live mutable latch set; falsified because a write during row construction changed membership evidence inside that single list.

payment_latch_validation_snapshot.claim: Capability inventory copies bounded exact-set payment-latch storage before iterating or validating its elements. Pre-copy and post-copy cardinality checks bound the snapshot, and later publications cannot resize the iterator or suppress the inventory receipt.
payment_latch_validation_snapshot.internal_measurement: A deterministic mutation after the first live-set element was consumed previously raised RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration and suppressed capability inventory. After repair, validation completes against the bounded copy while the publication remains visible only to later inventories.
payment_latch_validation_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Validating every element of the live exact set before copying is equivalent to validating the copy; falsified because a concurrent publication can resize the live iterator between those operations.

execution_latch_validation_snapshot.claim: Authenticated execution retains caller-owned exact-set storage only as the later latch publication target. Pre-route cardinality and element validation iterate a bounded copy, and route derives its state from a separate bounded snapshot, so a concurrent publication cannot resize the execution preflight iterator.
execution_latch_validation_snapshot.internal_measurement: A deterministic publication during the execution preflight previously raised RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration before opener access. After repair, the same mutation affects only the caller-owned source, validation completes on its copy, route snapshots the later state, and the valid request succeeds.
execution_latch_validation_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Inventory-only snapshot validation is sufficient because execute immediately calls route; falsified because execute performed a separate live-set element scan before route could establish its safe snapshot.

post_callback_latch_reauthorization.claim: Injected nonce and monotonic-clock functions are treated as executable caller code. After the final such pre-network callback returns bounded passive data, FRANK re-evaluates payment-latch state from the same environment snapshot before constructing or opening the request. A newly active hard stop, exhausted latch capacity or changed provider selection fails closed before network access.
post_callback_latch_reauthorization.internal_measurement: Deterministic nonce and monotonic-clock callbacks each inserted the selected provider's current budget-epoch latch after initial routing. Before repair, both authenticated opener paths ran and returned success. After repair, one bounded route snapshot following the last callback observes either mutation and raises payment_required_hard_stop_active with zero opener calls.
post_callback_latch_reauthorization.counterhypothesis: Reauthorization immediately after nonce generation closes every caller-code boundary before network; falsified because the injected monotonic clock still executed afterward and could activate the same latch while leaving that reauthorization stale.

post_network_payment_latch_publication.claim: A received HTTP 402 remains mandatory execution evidence even if caller-owned latch storage changes after authorization. Publication validates bounded snapshots before and after mutation, reports payment_latch_publication_failed when state cannot be safely committed, and receipt construction never performs live-container membership afterward.
post_network_payment_latch_publication.internal_measurement: On both ordinary-response and HTTPError paths, an opener inserted a hash-equal active string after preflight. Before repair its equality method raised during latch publication or final receipt membership and no receipt returned. After repair both paths return status 402 and payment_required_hard_stop, mark publication failure, and later routing rejects the corrupted storage before network.
post_network_payment_latch_publication.counterhypothesis: Pre-network exact-set and exact-string validation is sufficient for a caller-owned mutable latch throughout authenticated execution; falsified because the opener can mutate that shared set while the request is in flight.

failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.claim: If a received HTTP 402 cannot be safely committed to caller-owned latch storage, FRANK retains the exact provider and budget-epoch key in bounded process-local fallback state. Inventories using external storage merge validated snapshots of both stores, so repairing or clearing the external container cannot authorize a same-process replay.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.internal_measurement: After a deterministic post-authorization corruption made the primary latch write fail, clearing that external set previously allowed a second authenticated request in the same budget epoch. The repaired runtime reports publication failure plus an active fallback latch and rejects attempt two before opener access.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.uncertainty: The fallback is process-local and does not survive restart. Durable UnifiedDB-backed publication and an accepted Ubuntu live receipt remain required before claiming restart-level enforcement.
failed_payment_latch_process_fallback.counterhypothesis: Failing closed only while malformed caller storage remains present is equivalent to a current-epoch hard stop; falsified because the caller could clear the malformed element and immediately regain routing eligibility.

successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.claim: Every HTTP 402 latch safely published to caller-owned storage is also retained under the exact provider and budget-epoch key in the bounded process-local store. Inventories merge validated snapshots of both stores, so clearing an otherwise valid external set cannot authorize a same-process replay.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.internal_measurement: After a successful HTTP 402 publication to an exact caller-owned set, clearing that set previously allowed a second authenticated request in the same budget epoch. With process mirroring, the second attempt fails before opener access even though the external set is empty.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.uncertainty: The mirror is process-local and does not survive restart. Durable UnifiedDB-backed publication and an accepted Ubuntu live receipt remain required before claiming restart-level enforcement.
successful_payment_latch_process_mirror.counterhypothesis: A successful caller-owned latch write can be trusted for the lifetime of the execution process; falsified because the caller can clear the mutable set and immediately restore routing eligibility unless the observed HTTP 402 is independently mirrored.

post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.claim: On the regular-response HTTP 402 path, latch publication occurs only after the foreign response context has completed its __exit__ cleanup. The receipt therefore cannot claim an active payment hard stop that response cleanup subsequently erased before returning control to FRANK.
post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.internal_measurement: A deterministic response __exit__ cleared both caller-owned and process-local latch sets after the suite had published HTTP 402. Before repair, the first receipt still reported payment_latch_active=true while a second same-epoch request reached the opener. After repair, publication follows __exit__ and attempt two fails before network access.
post_cleanup_payment_latch_publication.counterhypothesis: Serializing the with suite through the execution lock makes latch publication inside that suite final; falsified because foreign __exit__ runs after the suite and can mutate shared latch storage before the with statement returns.

passive_payment_latch_container_boundary.claim: Every payment-latch storage path, including the process-global default and caller injection, must be an exact built-in set before capability inventory, routing or authenticated execution; set subclasses cannot execute overridden membership or mutation behavior around a received HTTP 402.
passive_payment_latch_container_boundary.counterhypothesis: The process-owned default can bypass the passive-container boundary because only caller-supplied state is untrusted; falsified locally because replacing that mutable module state with a set subclass executed overridden membership during ordinary routing and leaked its exception. Earlier executable evidence separately showed overridden add suppressing mandatory post-402 receipt publication.

passive_payment_latch_element_boundary.claim: Every caller-supplied payment-latch key must be an exact built-in string before capability inventory, routing or authenticated execution; a passive set container does not make polymorphic elements passive.
passive_payment_latch_element_boundary.counterhypothesis: An exact built-in set is sufficient to make membership and mutation passive; falsified locally because a contained str subclass executed overridden equality after both HTTP 402 transport paths and suppressed mandatory receipt publication.

execution_busy_timeout.claim: A caller waiting for the single-instance execution lock fails closed as execution_busy after 35 seconds and cannot reach credential use or network access.
execution_busy_timeout.counterhypothesis: An unbounded lock wait is acceptable because the active transport has its own timeout; falsified locally because a held execution lock blocked a waiting call indefinitely outside the transport timeout boundary.

passive_attempt_nonce_boundary.claim: An injected attempt nonce must be an exact built-in nonempty Unicode-scalar string of at most 128 characters before authenticated execution; string subclasses, lone UTF-16 surrogates and unbounded identity material are rejected before formatting or UTF-8 hashing so receipt identity cannot fail or allocate without bound after a provider request has already run.
passive_attempt_nonce_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any exact built-in nonempty Unicode-scalar str is safe bounded hash material; falsified locally because a 129-character injected nonce reached authenticated execution and post-response identity processing even though the production nonce is the documented 32 hexadecimal characters from token_hex(16).

receipt_clock_domains.claim: Execution receipt duration uses a monotonic clock that cannot move backwards, while an absolute Retry-After HTTP-date is compared with the wall-clock UTC instant at response receipt.
receipt_clock_domains.counterhypothesis: One wall clock is sufficient for both elapsed duration and absolute HTTP-date arithmetic; falsified because system-clock correction can make receipt duration move backwards or collapse to zero, while a monotonic clock has no UTC epoch for interpreting HTTP-date.

passive_monotonic_clock_boundary.claim: An injected monotonic clock must return an exact built-in finite float or integer before authenticated execution. Invalid start values fail before network access; invalid end values use zero duration and cannot suppress an execution receipt or run overloaded formatting and arithmetic methods.
passive_monotonic_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any float-like value returned by an injected monotonic clock is passive duration metadata; falsified locally because a float subclass reached authenticated execution and then ran overridden __format__ during attempt-ID construction, preventing the mandatory receipt.

bounded_receipt_duration.claim: Receipt duration arithmetic is total and capped at 86400000 milliseconds. Nonpositive elapsed values become zero; a positive subtraction overflow, non-finite difference or larger elapsed value reaches the cap without suppressing or bloating the execution receipt.
bounded_receipt_duration.counterhypothesis: Validating each injected monotonic reading as a finite built-in number is sufficient; falsified locally because two finite floats produced an infinite difference and OverflowError after successful execution, while two exact integers produced unbounded receipt metadata.

bounded_attempt_identity_clock_boundary.claim: Attempt identity is derived from the stable request ID and a fresh 128-bit nonce, never from decimal formatting of an unbounded injected clock integer. Clock values remain duration telemetry and cannot suppress the mandatory post-execution receipt.
bounded_attempt_identity_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Including the monotonic start value in the attempt-ID preimage adds harmless uniqueness; falsified locally because an exact passive integer exceeded Python's decimal-conversion limit only after successful provider execution and prevented the receipt, while the mandatory nonce already supplies attempt uniqueness.

passive_wall_clock_boundary.claim: An injected wall clock used for absolute Retry-After arithmetic must return an exact built-in finite float or integer. Invalid and polymorphic values use the conservative 60-second fallback without executing arithmetic methods, reclassifying HTTP 429 or suppressing its receipt.
passive_wall_clock_boundary.counterhypothesis: Any float-like wall-clock result is passive timestamp metadata for HTTP-date subtraction; falsified locally because a float subclass executed overridden __rsub__, downgraded the regular 429 path and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

text_message_roles.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; tool/function messages require the separate typed tool-calling path.
text_message_roles.counterhypothesis: An arbitrary nonempty role can be delegated to provider-side validation; falsified for this adapter because it causes an avoidable authenticated network call before the provider can reject it.

exact_model_identifier.claim: The model field must match the model identifier served by NVIDIA NIM exactly; leading or trailing whitespace is rejected before credential use or network access rather than silently normalized.
exact_model_identifier.counterhypothesis: Any nonblank model string can be delegated to provider-side validation or trimmed locally; falsified because leading, trailing and newline whitespace all reached the authenticated opener, while silent normalization would change request identity rather than validate the caller's exact identifier.

bearer_credential_syntax.claim: A configured provider credential is routable only when it is at most 8192 characters and matches the RFC 6750 b64token grammar before normalization, scanning or Authorization-header construction; oversized values, whitespace, CR/LF, non-ASCII and other separators fail closed before network access.
bearer_credential_syntax.counterhypothesis: A syntactically valid b64token is automatically bounded credential evidence and the HTTP stack can impose limits later; falsified because an 8193-character value was selected for authenticated routing and reached header construction, while the exact 8192-character policy boundary remains accepted.

incomplete_body_errors.claim: http.client.IncompleteRead after a received response is an incomplete provider response, not an unhandled process exception.
incomplete_body_errors.counterhypothesis: Timeout handling covers every interrupted body read; falsified because IncompleteRead is an HTTPException rather than TimeoutError or URLError and escaped without a receipt.

pre_response_disconnects.claim: A ConnectionError such as http.client.RemoteDisconnected before response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
pre_response_disconnects.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps remote disconnects in URLError; falsified by the executable opener path where RemoteDisconnected escaped directly without a receipt.

malformed_http_status.claim: A BadStatusLine before valid response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
malformed_http_status.counterhypothesis: Only timeout, URL and connection exceptions can occur before a response; falsified because BadStatusLine is an independent HTTPException and escaped without a receipt.

transport_os_errors.claim: Transport-layer OSError failures such as ssl.SSLError before response headers are unreachable provider attempts with null status and no EXECUTED state.
transport_os_errors.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps TLS failures in URLError or ConnectionError; falsified by the executable opener path where SSLError propagated directly without a receipt.

transport_post_replay_safety.claim: A Chat Completions POST with a transport or response-read failure is not automatically retryable unless the client can prove the original request was never applied or the operation is idempotent.
transport_post_replay_safety.counterhypothesis: No response bytes or an incomplete response proves the POST was not applied and makes blind retry safe; falsified because RemoteDisconnected describes failure while reading the response, and the adapter cannot observe whether the provider already processed the request.

generic_provider_error_replay_safety.claim: Generic 4xx and 5xx responses to a non-idempotent Chat Completions POST are not automatically retryable; a received status never proves replay safety.
generic_provider_error_replay_safety.counterhypothesis: Every non-429 provider error becomes safe to replay after a short cooldown; falsified because unchanged 4xx requests require request, credential or policy correction, while a 5xx response does not prove that the original POST had no application-side effects.

rate_limit_retry_after.claim: A received HTTP 429 Retry-After field controls when a later request may be attempted and is parsed in either delay-seconds or HTTP-date form across regular-response and HTTPError paths. Absolute HTTP-date cooldown is calculated from response receipt time, not request start; neither form authorizes automatic replay of the same non-idempotent POST.
rate_limit_retry_after.counterhypothesis: Retry-After both supplies the cooldown and proves that identical POST replay is safe, or an HTTP-date can be subtracted from request start; falsified because RFC 6585 only describes when to make a new request, RFC 9110 separately requires replay-safety evidence, and a 100-second request inflated a 40-second remaining window to 140 seconds.

oversized_retry_after.claim: Retry-After metadata is limited to 128 characters before normalization, digit scanning or HTTP-date parsing. Larger values use the conservative 60-second fallback and cannot impose unbounded post-response parsing work or suppress the received HTTP 429 receipt.
oversized_retry_after.counterhypothesis: An exact built-in string is bounded enough to pass to Retry-After parsers after a received response; falsified locally because a 129-character syntactically impossible value reached parsedate_to_datetime after HTTP 429. A 100-digit delay remains accepted and safely caps to 86400 seconds.

retry_after_header_access_failure.claim: Failure while reading Retry-After metadata from a transport adapter cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429; regular-response and HTTPError paths retain rate_limited plus EXECUTED and use the conservative 60-second fallback.
retry_after_header_access_failure.counterhypothesis: Header lookup is total once an adapter exposes a headers object; falsified by an injected mapping-compatible adapter whose get operation raises ValueError: the regular-response path changed 429 to invalid_provider_response and the HTTPError path escaped without a receipt.

passive_retry_after_value_boundary.claim: A Retry-After value returned by a transport adapter must be an exact built-in string before parsing; polymorphic string subclasses use the conservative 60-second fallback without executing overridden methods, reclassifying the received HTTP 429 or suppressing its receipt.
passive_retry_after_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, str) proves that a transport-provided Retry-After value is passive text; falsified locally because a str subclass executed its overridden strip method, downgraded a regular 429 to incomplete_provider_response and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

response_header_property_failure.claim: The transport adapter's headers attribute is optional metadata behind a potentially executable descriptor. Failure while retrieving that property cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429; both response forms use the 60-second fallback and retain EXECUTED.
response_header_property_failure.counterhypothesis: Catching failures from the header mapping's get method fully contains untrusted metadata access; falsified because a property descriptor can raise before a mapping object is returned, causing regular 429 misclassification and an escaped HTTPError path.

response_status_property_failure.claim: Status and code attributes supplied by a transport adapter are executable metadata lookups. If retrieval fails, the adapter emits invalid_provider_response with null status and without EXECUTED, rather than escaping without a receipt or inventing a status.
response_status_property_failure.counterhypothesis: Status and HTTPError code attributes are passive values and cannot fail during access; falsified by response and HTTPError property descriptors whose RuntimeError escaped both receipt paths.

passive_http_status_value_boundary.claim: HTTP status metadata must be an exact built-in integer before range or classification comparisons; boolean and polymorphic integer values fail closed with null status and without EXECUTED, and no overridden comparison operator may run.
passive_http_status_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, int) plus excluding bool proves that transport status is passive numeric metadata; falsified locally because an int subclass executed its overridden comparison operator, changed the regular response to unreachable_provider and escaped the HTTPError path without a receipt.

unexpected_transport_adapter_failure.claim: A custom transport adapter can raise an Exception outside urllib's documented hierarchy. The outer execution boundary emits unreachable_provider before a valid response or incomplete_provider_response after valid status metadata, remains nonretryable, and deliberately does not catch BaseException process-control signals.
unexpected_transport_adapter_failure.counterhypothesis: URLError, OSError and HTTPException cover every opener, context-manager and body-read failure; falsified by custom adapter RuntimeError before response and during body read, both of which escaped without receipts.

bounded_retry_after_cooldown.claim: Retry-After cooldown metadata is bounded to 86400 seconds in receipts for both delay-seconds and HTTP-date forms; the nonretryable request requires fresh operator or scheduler evaluation beyond that horizon.
bounded_retry_after_cooldown.counterhypothesis: Syntactically valid Retry-After values are inherently operationally bounded; falsified by a 100-digit delay and a year-9999 HTTP-date that produced unbounded receipt integers on both response paths.

http_status_validation.claim: A provider adapter must supply an integer HTTP status from 100 through 599 before the body is consumed or EXECUTED is asserted; missing, boolean, textual and out-of-range values are invalid.
http_status_validation.counterhypothesis: A missing adapter status can safely default to 200 and Python isinstance(value, int) is sufficient; falsified because missing status verified arbitrary content and bool is an int subclass.

http_response_body_type.claim: The HTTP adapter body must be bytes before JSON parsing; text and bytearray values are invalid transport responses even when they contain valid JSON.
http_response_body_type.counterhypothesis: Successful json.loads parsing proves a valid HTTP body; falsified because json.loads intentionally accepts str and bytearray in addition to bytes.

passive_http_response_body_boundary.claim: A transport-provided HTTP response body must be an exact built-in bytes value before size measurement or UTF-8 decoding; bytes subclasses remain invalid_provider_response and no overridden length or decode method may execute.
passive_http_response_body_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, bytes) proves that an adapter body is passive immutable transport data; falsified locally because a bytes subclass executed its overridden __len__ after HTTP 200 and changed invalid adapter metadata into incomplete_provider_response.

network_json_encoding.claim: Network-transmitted provider JSON is decoded strictly as UTF-8 before parsing; UTF-16 and UTF-32 response bodies cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
network_json_encoding.counterhypothesis: Passing response bytes directly to Python json.loads enforces the network JSON encoding contract; falsified because the decoder automatically recognized UTF-16 and UTF-32 bodies and both reached success, VERIFIED and DONE.

strict_json_numbers.claim: Provider response JSON containing NaN, Infinity, -Infinity or an exponent that overflows the runtime float range is invalid and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
strict_json_numbers.counterhypothesis: Rejecting the nonstandard NaN and Infinity literals through parse_constant is sufficient to keep non-finite values out; falsified because CPython decodes RFC-grammar exponents such as 1e400 through the separate default float path and produced infinity that reached success, VERIFIED and DONE.

unique_json_object_names.claim: Provider response objects with duplicate member names are ambiguous across parsers and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
unique_json_object_names.counterhypothesis: Python's last-name-wins behavior is a safe canonical interpretation; falsified as a portability claim because RFC 8259 documents error, last-only and all-pairs behaviors as interoperably unpredictable.

json_nesting_failure_receipts.claim: Excessively nested provider JSON that reaches Python's recursion limit must emit invalid_provider_response rather than escape without an execution receipt.
json_nesting_failure_receipts.counterhypothesis: The 2000000-byte response limit is sufficient to bound every JSON parser failure; falsified by a roughly 40000-byte, 20000-level array that raised RecursionError without a receipt.

unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.claim: Text-chat request and response strings must contain Unicode scalar values; lone UTF-16 surrogates cannot cross the authenticated request boundary or reach VERIFIED/DONE.
unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.counterhypothesis: Successful Python json.loads parsing proves an interoperable Unicode string; falsified because an escaped lone surrogate was decoded as str and reached success/VERIFIED/DONE even though RFC 8259 calls receiver behavior unpredictable.

plain_text_message_fields.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts exactly role and content in each message; tool_calls, tool_call_id, name, reasoning_content and future extension fields require an explicitly typed adapter.
plain_text_message_fields.counterhypothesis: Validating role and content is enough for a text-only adapter; falsified because an assistant message carrying tool_calls passed unchanged to the authenticated network opener.

nonempty_text_conversation.claim: NVIDIA Chat Completions requires messages to contain at least one item; an empty conversation is rejected before credential use or network access.
nonempty_text_conversation.counterhypothesis: Provider-side validation is sufficient; falsified because an empty messages list reached the authenticated opener and caused an avoidable network attempt.

nonblank_text_message_content.claim: Every role/content message handled by this plain-text adapter requires nonblank scalar text before credential use or network access. This is a fail-closed adapter rule, not an additional NVIDIA schema claim: empty content can have meaning only in typed tool or multimodal paths, which this adapter rejects separately.
nonblank_text_message_content.counterhypothesis: Provider-side validation or an empty text message is sufficient for this adapter; falsified locally because empty and whitespace-only user content both reached the authenticated opener despite carrying no typed tool or multimodal payload.

text_conversation_sequence.claim: NVIDIA Chat Completions requires user and assistant messages to alternate, the final input message to have role user, and an optional system message to be first; invalid sequences are rejected before credential use or network access.
text_conversation_sequence.counterhypothesis: Validating each role independently is sufficient; falsified because assistant-ended, consecutive-user and late-system conversations all reached the authenticated opener despite violating the documented conversation grammar.

plain_text_response_fields.claim: A text-only response message requires role assistant plus scalar content only; missing authorship, tool_calls and other typed response extensions cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE through this adapter.
plain_text_response_fields.counterhypothesis: A nonempty content string plus terminal finish reason is sufficient proof of a complete text response; falsified because both a response carrying tool_calls and a response without assistant authorship reached success/VERIFIED/DONE.

pending_http_results.claim: For NVIDIA Chat Completions, HTTP 200 is fulfilled while HTTP 202 is pending and requires requestId polling; a 202 response cannot reach VERIFIED/DONE or trigger a blind replay of the original request.
pending_http_results.counterhypothesis: Every 2xx response can be treated as a final chat completion; falsified because NVIDIA explicitly assigns pending semantics to 202 and a valid-looking 202 text body previously reached success/VERIFIED/DONE. Polling remains intentionally unsupported until a requestId-bound adapter exists.

unexpected_success_statuses.claim: For this NVIDIA Chat Completions POST, 200 is the only fulfilled final-text status and 202 is explicitly pending; any other 2xx proves execution but is nonfinal and nonretryable without operation-specific recovery evidence.
unexpected_success_statuses.counterhypothesis: An undocumented 201, 204 or 206 can be handled as a retryable provider error; falsified because RFC 9110 classifies every 2xx as successfully received, understood and accepted and warns against automatically retrying a non-idempotent POST without proof that replay is safe.

completion_finish_reason.claim: A non-streaming NVIDIA Chat Completions choice reaches final-text VERIFIED only with explicit finish_reason stop and nonblank final content; length is truncated and null is a nonterminal streaming-chunk state. Treating whitespace-only content as empty is this adapter's fail-closed operationalization of NVIDIA's non-empty-final-answer guidance, not an additional provider-schema claim.
completion_finish_reason.counterhypothesis: Either any nonempty assistant content string or finish_reason stop alone is sufficient evidence of a completed answer; falsified locally because length and null with partial text, stop with empty content, and stop with whitespace-only content all previously reached success, VERIFIED and DONE. The whitespace-only case could represent intentional formatting, but the plain-text adapter cannot distinguish that from a missing answer and therefore fails closed. Identical blind retry after length remains disabled because NVIDIA requires changing token limits or reasoning budget.

request_snapshot_boundary.claim: Mutable caller-owned message objects are snapshotted before validation, routing and authenticated request construction; only the validated snapshot may be serialized.
request_snapshot_boundary.counterhypothesis: Validating the caller's list once is sufficient because request construction follows immediately; falsified locally by a deterministic routing-side mutation that changed validated content to blank text and added an unvalidated tool_calls field before serialization.

authorization_environment_snapshot.claim: Execution snapshots only recognized provider-runtime environment inputs before routing and authorization; credential, endpoint, budget epoch and attestation values used by one attempt cannot change before authenticated request construction.
authorization_environment_snapshot.counterhypothesis: Reading the shared environment repeatedly is safe because request construction immediately follows routing; falsified locally when a deterministic post-authorization mutation replaced the credential that was actually sent.

capability_receipt_snapshot_consistency.claim: A capability receipt snapshots recognized process-environment inputs once, computes one inventory and derives its route directly from those same rows. Inventory and route therefore describe one capability state rather than two observation times.
capability_receipt_snapshot_consistency.counterhypothesis: Two immediate environment snapshots are equivalent for a capability receipt; falsified locally when the first snapshot observed a configured provider while the second did not, yielding configured=true in inventory and selected=null in the same receipt.

environment_snapshot_exception_redaction.claim: Failures from a runtime-environment adapter are collapsed to a constant fail-closed error outside the active exception handler; arbitrary adapter text is neither displayed nor retained as __context__ or __cause__, and network access remains impossible.
environment_snapshot_exception_redaction.counterhypothesis: Catching only common mapping failures or chaining the original exception is safe; falsified because LookupError escaped verbatim with credential-like text before network access, while raising inside the handler would retain the original as exception context.

passive_environment_value_boundary.claim: Runtime capability inputs must be exact built-in strings before entering the environment snapshot; string subclasses are active objects whose overridden methods must never execute during routing, attestation or credential processing.
passive_environment_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: isinstance(value, str) proves that an environment value is passive text; falsified locally because a str subclass passed that check, its overridden split method executed after the snapshot and leaked credential-like exception text before network access.

bounded_runtime_policy_value_boundary.claim: Recognized host-policy strings are cardinality-bounded during the environment snapshot before normalization, URL parsing, hashing or list splitting: the local-test flag is limited to 1 character, the budget epoch to 256, the zero-cost attestation list to 1024 and the provider base URL to 2048. These are local FRANK resource budgets, not external protocol limits; credentials retain their separate 8192-character bearer-token boundary.
bounded_runtime_policy_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: Exact built-in strings are intrinsically bounded passive policy data; falsified locally because a 1400-character attestation reached str.split and allocated its complete parsed list on every route, including the process-serialized execution path.

passive_text_request_value_boundary.claim: Model identifiers, message roles and message content must be exact built-in strings before validation or JSON serialization; string subclasses are active objects and are rejected before any overridden method, credential lookup or network operation can run.
passive_text_request_value_boundary.counterhypothesis: String subclasses are equivalent to passive JSON text because isinstance(value, str) succeeds; falsified locally for model, role and content because each accepted subclass executed its overridden strip method and leaked exception text before routing.

passive_text_request_container_boundary.claim: The text request snapshot accepts only exact built-in list and dict containers with exact built-in string field names; container subclasses are rejected before iteration, mapping conversion, validation, credential lookup or serialization.
passive_text_request_container_boundary.counterhypothesis: A list subclass is passive request data because isinstance(messages, list) succeeds; falsified locally because tuple(messages) invoked its overridden __iter__, whose LookupError and credential-like text escaped before routing.

wide_message_pre_snapshot_boundary.claim: An exact built-in message dict whose cardinality differs from the closed two-field role/content schema is rejected with passive len checks before execution-lock acquisition and again immediately before snapshot copying. Structurally impossible wide objects are never duplicated by dict(message).
wide_message_pre_snapshot_boundary.counterhypothesis: Snapshotting before schema validation is memory-safe because the outer message list is cardinality-bounded; falsified locally because one exact dict with 10002 fields was fully copied under the execution lock before its impossible field set was rejected.

response_context_cleanup_boundary.claim: A valid non-200 HTTP status is classified and its safety effects are committed before response-context cleanup; an Exception raised by adapter __exit__ cannot downgrade an already classified HTTP 402 or remove its payment latch.
response_context_cleanup_boundary.counterhypothesis: The generic adapter Exception fallback is sufficient after any valid status; falsified locally because a context-manager __exit__ RuntimeError changed a received HTTP 402 into incomplete_provider_response and left the payment latch inactive.

response_size_context_suppression_bounda.claim: Response-size overflow is recorded as state inside the foreign response context and classified outside it; adapter __exit__ cannot suppress or downgrade a MAX+1 overflow.
response_size_context_suppression_bounda.counterhypothesis: Raising ProviderResponseTooLarge inside with is sufficient; falsified because __exit__ returning true suppressed it and an exact MAX+1-byte valid JSON body reached success, VERIFIED and DONE.

response_context_suite_exception_boundar.claim: Normal exceptions raised while validating metadata or consuming a response are captured inside the foreign context and re-raised only after cleanup, so adapter __exit__ cannot suppress the evidence required for fail-closed receipt classification.
response_context_suite_exception_boundar.counterhypothesis: An outer try/except around with is sufficient to preserve every receipt; falsified because a true __exit__ suppressed missing-status validation, left outcome undefined and caused UnboundLocalError outside the receipt boundary.

response_context_process_control_boundar.claim: BaseException process-control signals raised in the foreign response suite are transported across cleanup and immediately re-raised unchanged; adapter __exit__ cannot suppress them and they are never converted into execution receipts.
response_context_process_control_boundar.counterhypothesis: Catching only Exception inside the suite preserves deliberate BaseException propagation; falsified because a true __exit__ suppressed SystemExit and execution continued as a normal incomplete-provider receipt.

invariants: Never serialize, log, commit, echo or display API secret values.
Never access Together, including discovery, probes, routing and fallback.
Never make a paid request unless the project owner separately authorizes a nonzero budget.
A configured key is capability evidence, not proof of quota or health.

A provider credential is limited to 8192 characters and must match RFC 6750 b64token syntax before it can become configured capability evidence or enter an Authorization header; oversized values, whitespace, control characters, non-ASCII and separators fail closed before network access.
Except for an officially documented free developer endpoint, a configured key requires explicit host-side zero-cost attestation before routing.
A provider credential may only be sent to that provider's canonical host; a global multi-provider host allowlist is forbidden.
Credential binding compares the full remote origin boundary, including the effective HTTPS port; hostname equality alone is insufficient.
Provider endpoint URLs containing userinfo are rejected before request construction or network access.
Authenticated provider requests must not follow HTTP redirects; redirects fail closed before credentials can cross an origin boundary.

The text-chat adapter validates an exact nonblank model identifier plus object messages with nonempty string roles and nonblank scalar string content before network access; typed tool or multimodal requests require a separate adapter.

The serialized UTF-8 text-chat JSON request is at most 2000000 bytes; oversized payloads fail before runtime-environment snapshot, credential lookup or network access, while the exact boundary remains accepted.

Every Chat Completions request explicitly sets max_tokens to 4096, bounding the combined reasoning and visible generation budget; finish_reason length remains unverified and requires changed input or budget rather than blind replay.

Requests above the transport envelope are rejected before json.dumps can materialize the document; the preflight exactly counts the fixed request envelope, per-message objects, list separators and default ensure_ascii escape widths, while the serialized UTF-8 byte check remains defense in depth.

For exact built-in request strings, a character-count lower bound above 2000000 rejects before the process execution lock; unavoidable oversized text cannot consume serialized routing capacity while awaiting the later exact JSON calculation.

Exact built-in message lists above 54792 entries are rejected before caller-data snapshotting and before the process execution lock because required role alternation, separators and envelope structure prove that no valid conversation of that cardinality can fit 2000000 bytes.
The message-cardinality bound is rechecked at the snapshot boundary so mutation after early admission cannot turn a small caller-owned list into an oversized allocation under the execution lock.

Exact built-in message objects whose cardinality differs from the two-field role/content schema are rejected before lock acquisition and rechecked immediately before snapshot copying; wide caller dicts are never duplicated under the execution lock.
Text-chat model, role and content values are exact built-in strings; polymorphic string subclasses fail closed before their methods, credential lookup, JSON serialization or network access can run.

Text-chat messages and message objects are exact built-in list and dict containers with exact built-in string field names; polymorphic container subclasses fail closed before iteration or mapping behavior can run.
The text-chat request contains at least one message; empty conversations are rejected before routing, credential use or network access.
The text-chat adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; arbitrary and tool/function roles are rejected before routing, credential use or network access.

The text-chat conversation optionally starts with one system message, then alternates user and assistant roles beginning and ending with user; invalid sequences are rejected before routing, credential use or network access.
Each plain-text message contains exactly role and content; extension fields such as tool_calls are rejected before routing, credential use or network access and require a typed adapter.
Caller-owned mutable messages are copied before validation; routing and concurrent mutations cannot change the validated request snapshot that is serialized.
Each execution snapshots only recognized runtime environment fields before routing; the credential and cost-policy inputs authorized for an attempt are the same values used to construct its request.

Each capability receipt uses one recognized environment snapshot and derives route directly from its inventory rows; configured capability evidence and selected route cannot represent different observation times.

Runtime-environment adapter failures collapse to one constant error outside the active handler; arbitrary adapter exception text is not displayed or retained, and no credential or network boundary is crossed.

Recognized runtime-environment values are exact built-in strings; polymorphic string subclasses fail closed before their methods can execute in capability inventory, routing, attestation or credential handling.

Recognized host-policy values are bounded in the runtime-environment snapshot before normalization, hashing, URL parsing or splitting; oversized values fail closed, while bearer credentials retain their separate 8192-character validation boundary.
The v0.1 execution path is process-serialized from routing through receipt publication so a payment-required latch from one attempt is visible before another attempt can route or reach the network.

All payment-latch storage, including the process-global default and caller injection, is an exact built-in set containing only exact built-in strings before capability inventory or routing; polymorphic container or element behavior cannot suppress a received HTTP 402 hard stop or its mandatory receipt.
Waiting for the v0.1 single-instance execution lock is bounded to 35 seconds; timeout raises execution_busy before routing, credential use or network access.
Execution receipt request IDs bind provider, endpoint host and serialized request digest and remain stable across retries; attempt IDs are unique per execution attempt.
Attempt IDs include a fresh high-entropy nonce so equal-time concurrent attempts cannot alias; raw nonces are never serialized.

Attempt-ID construction never decimal-formats injected clock values; request ID plus the fresh 128-bit nonce supply bounded identity material so extreme passive integers cannot suppress a post-execution receipt.

Attempt nonces are exact built-in nonempty Unicode-scalar strings of at most 128 characters before authenticated execution; polymorphic formatting, unbounded identity processing or post-request UTF-8 encoding failure cannot suppress the mandatory receipt.
A response reaches VERIFIED only when choices is a non-empty list whose first message is an object with string content; malformed JSON shapes fail closed with a receipt.
A choice explicitly finished because of length remains EXECUTED as provider_output_truncated, is nonretryable without a changed token budget, and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
A non-streaming text choice requires explicit finish_reason stop before VERIFIED or DONE; null, missing and unsupported finish reasons remain invalid_provider_response.
A stopped non-streaming text choice requires nonblank scalar content before VERIFIED or DONE; empty and whitespace-only final content remain invalid_provider_response.
The text-only response adapter requires role assistant plus content; missing authorship, tool_calls, reasoning_content and other typed extensions cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
An HTTP status response, including 429 and 5xx, proves EXECUTED transport but never VERIFIED or DONE; connection and timeout failures without an HTTP response remain unexecuted.
Every received non-2xx status remains unverified even when the transport returns it as a regular response object instead of raising HTTPError.

Only HTTP 200 is final for this NVIDIA text-completion path; HTTP 202 remains EXECUTED as provider_result_pending, cannot reach VERIFIED/DONE, and is not blindly replayed without a requestId-bound polling adapter.
Unexpected 2xx statuses remain EXECUTED as unexpected_success_status, cannot reach VERIFIED/DONE, and are nonretryable because the POST may already have been accepted.

Before body consumption or EXECUTED, adapter status must be an exact built-in integer in the RFC 9110 range 100 through 599; booleans, polymorphic integers and other invalid values remain null and invalid_provider_response without executing comparison operators.

Failure while retrieving a transport adapter's status or code property emits invalid_provider_response with null status and without EXECUTED; it cannot escape the receipt path or invent an HTTP result.
Unexpected Exception subclasses from custom transport adapters emit a fail-closed receipt based on whether valid response status was observed; BaseException control signals remain uncaught.

A received adapter body must be exact built-in bytes before size measurement or JSON parsing; text, bytearray, polymorphic bytes and other body types remain EXECUTED with their valid status but cannot execute body methods or reach VERIFIED/DONE.
Network-transmitted provider JSON must decode strictly as UTF-8 before parsing; UTF-16, UTF-32 and malformed UTF-8 remain invalid_provider_response and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.

Provider response JSON rejects every non-finite decoded number; NaN/Infinity literals and finite-syntax exponents that overflow the runtime float range remain invalid_provider_response and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Every provider JSON object must have unique member names; duplicates remain invalid_provider_response and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
JSON parser RecursionError after a valid response remains EXECUTED with its status, emits invalid_provider_response, and never escapes the receipt path or reaches VERIFIED or DONE.
Text-chat model, role, request content and verified response content contain only Unicode scalar values; lone UTF-16 surrogates are rejected before network or VERIFIED/DONE.
Malformed bodies preserve the received HTTP status and classify as invalid_provider_response; connection or timeout failures without a response use null status and unreachable_provider.
ConnectionError failures before response headers, including RemoteDisconnected, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED.
HTTPException failures before valid response headers, including BadStatusLine, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED.

Transport OSError failures before response headers, including SSLError, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED; after response headers they preserve status and EXECUTED as incomplete_provider_response.
A received non-200 status is classified directly from response metadata without consuming its body; in particular, HTTP 402 activates the payment hard stop even if its body would stall.
A valid non-200 status is classified before response-context cleanup; a normal Exception from adapter __exit__ cannot downgrade that received HTTP evidence or undo an HTTP 402 payment latch.
For HTTP 200, body-read failures after response headers preserve that status and EXECUTED while classifying as incomplete_provider_response; they never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Transport and response-read failures for the Chat Completions POST are nonretryable without provider-supported idempotency or proof that the original request was never applied.
A truncated HTTP body raising IncompleteRead preserves the received status and EXECUTED, emits an incomplete_provider_response receipt, and never reaches VERIFIED or DONE.
Provider responses larger than 2000000 bytes are detected with a one-byte sentinel read, classified as provider_response_too_large, and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Response-size overflow is carried beyond the foreign response context before classification; adapter __exit__ cannot suppress a MAX+1 overflow or allow oversized content into VERIFIED or DONE.
Response-suite Exceptions are captured before foreign context cleanup and classified afterward; adapter __exit__ cannot suppress invalid-status, body-type or body-read evidence needed for a receipt.
Response-suite BaseException signals cross foreign cleanup only to be re-raised unchanged; they cannot be suppressed by adapter __exit__ or converted into receipts.
Every real provider request must emit a redacted execution receipt.

No received non-2xx status automatically authorizes replay of the Chat Completions POST; replay requires changed input, operator recovery, provider-supported idempotency or proof that the original request was not applied.

A valid Retry-After field on HTTP 429 determines cooldown for a later request in either delay-seconds or HTTP-date form; absolute dates are measured from response receipt rather than request start, absent or invalid fields use the conservative 60-second fallback, and the same POST remains nonretryable.
Receipt duration is measured on a monotonic clock, while absolute Retry-After HTTP-date cooldown uses the wall-clock UTC instant at response receipt.

Injected monotonic-clock readings are exact built-in finite numbers before use; an invalid start fails before network and an invalid post-response reading falls back to zero duration without suppressing the receipt.
Receipt duration metadata is clamped to 0 through 86400000 milliseconds; arithmetic overflow, a non-finite positive difference or extreme exact integers cannot suppress or bloat a mandatory receipt.

Injected wall-clock readings used for Retry-After HTTP-date arithmetic are exact built-in finite numbers; invalid or polymorphic readings use the 60-second fallback without executing arithmetic methods or losing the received 429 receipt.

Retry-After metadata longer than 128 characters uses the 60-second fallback before normalization or parsing; oversized foreign metadata cannot impose unbounded post-response work, escape or suppress the execution receipt.
Failure to access Retry-After metadata uses the 60-second fallback and cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429 execution receipt.

Retry-After values returned by transport adapters are exact built-in strings before parsing; polymorphic values use the 60-second fallback without executing methods or reclassifying an already received HTTP 429.
Failure while retrieving an adapter's headers property uses the 60-second fallback and cannot suppress or reclassify an already received HTTP 429 execution receipt.
Retry-After receipt cooldown metadata is capped at 86400 seconds for both delay-seconds and HTTP-date forms; the request remains nonretryable and requires fresh evaluation after the bounded horizon.
Rate limits and provider faults trigger bounded cooldown and rerouting, never retry storms.
